```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup: read the caches"
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
# Code is shown (folded) in the HTML version and hidden in the PDF.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = knitr::is_html_output())
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

bridge = readRDS(file.path("data", "epo-bet-ss3-bridge-cache.rds"))
opal_c = readRDS(file.path("data", "epo-bet-opal-cache.rds"))

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
fmt = function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","))
sci = function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = d)
pct = function(x, d = 0) paste0(fmt(100 * x, d), "%")

B = bridge$summary
S = opal_c$summary
G = opal_c$growth_fit
TM = opal_c$timing
qtr_to_year = function(q) 1975 + (q - 17) / 4
model_col = c("SS3 B1" = "grey20", O0 = "#7D3C98", O1 = "#2471A3", O2 = "#C0392B",
              `O1-noComp` = "#CA6F1E", `O1-F` = "#17A589")
fleets = opal_c$fleets
```

# Overview

This document bridges an exploratory Stock Synthesis [SS3, @methot2013ss]
assessment model of bigeye tuna (*Thunnus obesus*) in the eastern Pacific
Ocean (EPO), prepared by IATTC staff for the 14th meeting of the IATTC
Scientific Advisory Committee [SAC-14, @iattc2023sac14bet], to opal. Any
model runs here are preliminary explorations and should not be used *as is*
for management advice.

The baseline SS3 model is itself a simplification. The models in the IATTC's
risk analysis for EPO bigeye have two sexes and time-varying selectivity;
the model used here has one sex and time-invariant selectivity, so that its
structure is close to what opal can represent. Its results are not those of
the risk-analysis models, and differences between SS3 and opal found here
say nothing about how opal would compare with them.

* **The model is quarterly.** Each SS3 "year" is a quarter (17-204, taken as
  1975 Q1 to 2021 Q4) and ages are quarters (0-40). opal takes the same
  layout: 188 time steps of one season and 41 ages.
* **One SS3 bridge step.** The supplied model (B0) estimates a regime offset
  on the initial equilibrium recruitment, which opal does not have; B1
  removes it (@sec-bridge). Growth needs no step: SS3's growth cessation
  model [@maunder2018growth] and its SD-linear growth variability are both
  in opal, and the conversion reproduces SS3's length-at-age and SD-at-age
  exactly below the plus group (@sec-growth).
* **The inputs reconcile; the dynamics differ.** The converted inputs
  reconcile with SS3 within the tolerances of @tbl-recon, and opal at SS3's
  parameter values matches an independent replay of the converted inputs,
  so the gap between opal and SS3 lies in the dynamics. opal removes each quarter's catch at
  the start of the quarter, as a harvest rate, while SS3 removes it through
  the quarter. With M of 0.48 per quarter at age 0 and large purse-seine
  catches of young fish, that leaves far more fish alive in opal
  (@sec-o0). Catch timing is the largest difference between the two models
  for this stock.
* **opal fits** (@sec-fits) estimate the scale and recruitment with SS3's
  selectivity held fixed (O1) and with opal's own double normals (O2).
* **Initial F** (@sec-init-f). SS3 fixes the initial F of the two fleets with
  an initial equilibrium catch (LL-n-A2 and OBJ-A5). Estimating them adds
  nothing with the regime offset on (B0-F). Without it (B1-F) the initial F
  of OBJ-A5 takes over much of the offset's job and brings SS3 back close to
  B0, but in opal (O1-F) it stays near 0 and changes almost nothing.

# The model {#sec-model}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fleets
#| tbl-cap: "Fisheries and data in opal (SS3 fleet numbers are kept). Units: catch in weight (1) or numbers (2). Compositions: the variance adjustment is opal's divisor of the input sample size, the inverse of SS3's multiplier."
knitr::kable(fleets[, .(`opal fishery` = fishery, `SS3 fleet` = ss3_fleet, name,
                        `catch units` = units, compositions = comps,
                        `variance adjustment` = fmt(var_adjust, 2))], format = "pipe")
```

* **Fisheries.** Longline fisheries in seven areas, with catch in numbers
  (LL-n) and in weight (LL-w; their selectivity mirrors the LL-n fishery of
  the same area); floating-object purse seine in five areas (OBJ) and its
  discards (OBJ-Disc, age-based selectivity of 1 at ages 1-3 quarters);
  unassociated purse seine in two areas (NOA, mirroring OBJ-A1 and OBJ-A5).
* **Index.** One longline index (LL-Survey, numbers, lognormal), with its own
  double-normal selectivity and SS3's floating catchability.
* **Compositions.** OBJ length compositions on 2 cm bins (20-198 cm); the
  longline fisheries' and the index's compositions are SS3 generalised size
  compositions on 10 cm bins (60-190 cm). In opal they are two composition
  bin schemes predicted from the same 2 cm population grid. SS3 gives zero
  weight to the NOA length compositions, LL-n-A1's size compositions and a
  handful of conditional age-at-length records, which are left out.
* **Biology.** Age-specific M (0.48 per quarter at age 0, falling to 0.10 at
  age 13 and rising to 0.14 from age 26), growth cessation, length-based
  maturity, spawning output proportional to weight (Nsexes = -1, female
  fraction 0.5), Beverton-Holt recruitment with steepness 1 and sigma~R~ 0.6.

# The SS3 bridge {#sec-bridge}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "The SS3 bridge. Negative log-likelihoods; SSB in tonnes; depletion and F/F~MSY~ in the last quarter (2021 Q4)."
knitr::kable(B[, .(step = label, `n par` = n_par, NLL = fmt(nll, 2), survey = fmt(nll_survey, 2),
                   length = fmt(nll_length, 2), `size freq.` = fmt(nll_sizefreq, 2),
                   recruitment = fmt(nll_recruit, 2), `ln R0` = fmt(ln_r0, 3),
                   `regime offset` = fmt(regime, 3), `SSB0` = fmt(ssb0, 0),
                   depletion = fmt(depletion, 3), `F/Fmsy` = fmt(f_end, 2),
                   `max gradient` = sci(max_gradient, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bridge
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass relative to unfished in the two SS3 bridge models."
ggplot(bridge$timeseries[era == "TIME"], aes(year, depletion, colour = label)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey20", "#2471A3")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SSB / SSB0", colour = NULL)
```

The supplied files were run with an SS3 3.30.22 beta build. Re-run with SS3
3.30.22.1 from the supplied parameters, B0 reproduces the supplied
likelihood exactly (`r fmt(bridge$supplied_likelihood[component == "TOTAL", logL_lambda], 3)`)
and re-estimation stays there.

```{r}
#| label: regime
tsw = dcast(bridge$timeseries[era == "TIME"], quarter + year ~ step, value.var = "ssb")
setnames(tsw, c("quarter", "year", "b0", "b1"))
tsw[, rel := b1 / b0 - 1]
mid = tsw[year >= 1980 & year < 2011, range(rel)]
```

B0 starts the population from an equilibrium whose recruitment is
`r fmt(100 * (1 - exp(B[1, regime])), 0)`% below the stock-recruitment curve
(a regime offset of `r fmt(B[1, regime], 2)` on ln R~0~ for block year 16,
the quarter before the model starts). The model begins in 1975 although
longline fishing on the stock goes back decades (the data file carries
catches for 1971-1974 that SS3 ignores, and the initial F is fixed at almost
0), and the offset is what lets the 1975 population start below its unfished
level: it scales every initial age class by exp(`r fmt(B[1, regime], 2)`).
SS3's lambda on the regime penalty is 0, so the offset is informed by the
data alone; SS3 estimates it at `r fmt(B[1, regime], 2)` (SE
`r fmt(B[1, regime_se], 2)`).

B1 removes it. The initial equilibrium recruitment is then tied to the
unfished stock-recruitment relationship, while the 24 penalised early
recruitment deviations can still alter the initial age structure; they take
over part of the offset's job (their mean is `r fmt(B[2, early_dev_mean], 2)`
in B1 against `r fmt(B[1, early_dev_mean], 2)` in B0). The likelihood worsens by `r fmt(B[2, nll] - B[1, nll], 1)`
units, and the difference does not wash out: B1's spawning biomass is
`r pct(tsw$rel[1])` above B0's in 1975 Q1, `r pct(mid[1])` to
`r pct(mid[2])` above it from 1980 to 2010, and `r pct(tail(tsw$rel, 1))` above
it in 2021 Q4 (depletion `r fmt(B[2, depletion], 3)` against
`r fmt(B[1, depletion], 3)`). opal is converted from B1, so the comparison
in the rest of this document is with a model whose trajectory differs from
the supplied one by this much (@sec-limitations).

# Converting B1 to opal {#sec-conversion}

`config/epo-bet-b1.yaml` records the choices the SS3 files do not determine.
The opal model has:

* 188 quarterly time steps, one season each, ages 0-40 quarters;
* 23 fisheries: SS3's 22 fishing fleets in SS3 order and one fishery for the
  index;
* SS3's age-basis biology (M, maturity, and spawning output) from the
  endgrowth table at the start of the quarter, and SS3's *mid*-quarter
  weight-at-age, which opal uses to turn catch in weight into numbers
  (@sec-o0);
* SS3's parameter values: B~0~ (opal's scale parameter, SS3's SSB~0~), h,
  sigma~R~, the main and late recruitment deviations, the 24 early deviations
  and the first quarter's recruitment as the initial age structure, the
  initial F of LL-n-A2 and OBJ-A5, and SS3's growth.

## Reconciliation

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recon
#| tbl-cap: "Reconciliation with SS3 (exact comparisons). The 22 catch totals are summarised in one row."
R = copy(opal_c$recon)[!is.na(pass)]
R[, group := ifelse(grepl("^catch total", quantity), "catch totals, 22 fishing fleets", quantity)]
knitr::kable(R[, .(n = .N, `max relative difference` = sci(max(rel_diff, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
                   pass = all(pass)), by = .(Quantity = group)], format = "pipe")
```

All `r nrow(opal_c$checks)` structural checks pass. The unfished spawning
potential per recruit reconciles to
`r sci(R[grepl("unfished", quantity)]$rel_diff, 1)`, which confirms the units
of M, the female fraction and the plus group in one number.

## Growth {#sec-growth}

SS3's growth cessation model (GrowthModel 8) is Eq. 2 of
@maunder2018growth, which opal implements as `growth_model = "cessation"`.
The parameters map directly:

| SS3 | Value | opal |
|---|---|---|
| L at age 0 (AFIX = 0) | `r fmt(G$L0, 2)` cm | `L0` |
| rmax (labelled VonBert_K) | `r fmt(G$rmax, 4)` cm per quarter | `rmax` |
| Cessation | `r fmt(G$k_gc, 4)` | `k_gc` |
| Linf (Growth_Age_for_L2 = 999) | `r fmt(G$Linf, 3)` cm | `t50` = `r fmt(G$t50, 3)` quarters, as SS3 computes it from Linf |
| SS3 age 0 = opal position 1 | | `age_offset` = `r G$age_offset` |

SS3's CV_Growth_Pattern 2 makes the SD of length-at-age linear in mean
length, from `r fmt(G$v1, 2)` cm at L~0~ to `r fmt(G$v2, 2)` cm at Linf;
opal's `growth_sd_model = "sd"` does the same. Linf is not a modelled
length, so opal's upper reference is the mean length at the oldest age, with
the SD SS3's line takes there (`r fmt(G$v2_at_oldest, 3)` cm).

```{r}
#| label: fig-growth
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Mean and SD of length-at-age: SS3 (Report.sso, start of the quarter) and opal."
gd = data.table(age = 0:40, ss3_mean = G$laa_ss3, opal_mean = G$laa_opal,
                ss3_sd = G$sd_ss3, opal_sd = G$sd_opal)
gl = rbind(gd[, .(age, what = "mean length (cm)", model = "SS3", value = ss3_mean)],
           gd[, .(age, what = "mean length (cm)", model = "opal", value = opal_mean)],
           gd[, .(age, what = "SD of length (cm)", model = "SS3", value = ss3_sd)],
           gd[, .(age, what = "SD of length (cm)", model = "opal", value = opal_sd)])
ggplot(gl, aes(age, value, colour = model, linetype = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~what, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(SS3 = "grey20", opal = "#C0392B")) +
    labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

Below the plus group opal's length-at-age matches SS3's to
`r sci(G$max_rel_error_below_plus, 1)` and its SD to
`r sci(G$sd_max_rel_error_below_plus, 1)` (relative), the precision of
Report.sso. At the plus group SS3 averages length over the ages it
accumulates (`r fmt(tail(G$laa_ss3, 1), 2)` cm against opal's
`r fmt(tail(G$laa_opal, 1), 2)` cm) and holds the SD at SD_old itself.

## Selectivity

SS3's selectivity is size-based, like opal's, so its double normals carry
over rather than being fitted. Two details are converted:

* SS3 places the end of the plateau relative to the midpoint of its last
  *population* length bin (221 cm), opal relative to its last data length
  bin (199 cm). opal's top parameter is re-solved so the plateau ends where
  SS3's does.
* Where SS3 sets a start or end parameter to -999 (no rescaling of that
  limb), opal's end value is set to the value SS3's unscaled limb takes at
  the first or last bin.

OBJ-Disc's selectivity is on age in SS3 (1 at ages 1-3 quarters, 0
elsewhere); in opal it is an age-based double normal fitted to that and
held fixed.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-seed
#| tbl-cap: "Largest difference between opal's starting selectivity and SS3's: at length for the length-based fisheries (mirrors take their source fleet's parameters), at age for OBJ-Disc."
sc = copy(opal_c$seed_check)
knitr::kable(sc[, .(`opal fishery` = fishery, name, `parameters from` = ifelse(is.na(source), "age-based fit", as.character(source)),
                    `max |diff|` = sci(max_abs_diff, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

Every fleet's SS3 age selectivity (pattern 10) is 0 at age 0. opal applies
its length curves to every age through the PLA, so the OBJ fisheries select
some age-0 fish in opal that SS3 does not; at the start of the quarter an
age-0 fish is `r fmt(G$laa_ss3[1], 1)` cm. SS3 also evaluates fishery
selectivity on the mid-quarter size distribution, opal at the start of the
quarter. Both show in opal's starting selectivity-at-age:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sel-age
#| tbl-cap: "Largest difference between opal's starting selectivity-at-age (O2 before fitting) and SS3's, and opal's selectivity at age 0, by fishery."
knitr::kable(opal_c$sel_start_diff[, .(fishery, name, `max |diff|` = fmt(max_abs_diff, 3),
                                        `opal at age 0` = fmt(age0_opal, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

## opal at SS3's values {#sec-o0}

O0 runs opal at SS3's parameter values with SS3's own selectivity-at-age.
Nothing is estimated, so any difference from SS3 comes from the two models'
dynamics. To find out which part of the dynamics, this section compares
both models with a set of *replays*.

### How the replays work {#sec-replays}

A replay is a short population projection written in plain R (in
`scripts/02-convert-fit-epo-bet-opal.r`), outside both opal and SS3. It
estimates nothing. It takes a fixed set of inputs, all at SS3 B1's values,
and steps the population forward one quarter at a time:

* the numbers-at-age in 1975 Q1 (opal's, which equal SS3's to
  `r pct(abs(opal_c$bridge$rel_opal[1]), 2)` in spawning biomass);
* the recruitment in each quarter, R~0~ exp(dev~y~ − b~y~ σ~R~^2^ / 2), with
  SS3's deviations dev~y~ and bias adjustment b~y~ (steepness is 1, so
  recruitment does not depend on spawning biomass);
* M-at-age, spawning output-at-age, and SS3's selectivity-at-age s~f,a~
  for each fleet f;
* the observed catch C~f,y~ of each fleet in each quarter.

In each quarter the replay records spawning biomass, Σ~a~ N~a~ × spawning
output~a~, then takes the quarter's catch out of the numbers-at-age N~a~,
applies natural mortality, moves every age class up one quarter (the oldest
stays in the plus group), and adds the next quarter's recruits. The replays
differ only in how the catch comes out, which is the one step where opal
and SS3 differ:

* **Start of quarter** (opal's `do_dynamics()`): each fleet's catch is a
  harvest rate on the numbers at the start of the quarter, taken before any
  natural mortality, and the survivors then die at rate M:
  $$h_{f,a} = \frac{C_f\, s_{f,a}}{\sum_{a'} N_{a'}\, s_{f,a'}\, w_{f,a'}}, \qquad
    N_a' = N_a \Big(1 - \sum_f h_{f,a}\Big)\, e^{-M_a}.$$
* **Mid-quarter** (Pope's approximation): half the quarter's natural
  mortality, then the same harvest rate taken from what is left, then the
  other half: $N_a' = \big(N_a e^{-M_a/2}\big)\big(1 - \sum_f h_{f,a}\big) e^{-M_a/2}$,
  with $h_{f,a}$ computed from $N_a e^{-M_a/2}$.
* **Through the quarter** (the Baranov catch equation): fishing and natural
  mortality act together all quarter, and each fleet's F~f~ is solved so
  that its predicted catch matches the observed one, which is what SS3's
  hybrid F method does:
  $$C_f = \sum_a \frac{F_f\, s_{f,a}}{Z_a}\, N_a \big(1 - e^{-Z_a}\big)\, w_{f,a}, \qquad
    Z_a = M_a + \sum_f F_f\, s_{f,a}, \qquad N_a' = N_a e^{-Z_a}.$$

For fleets whose catch is in weight, w~f,a~ turns tonnes into numbers. It
is one of three weights: start-of-quarter weight; mid-quarter weight (the
one vector opal uses here); or each fleet's own catch weight-at-age from
SS3 (Report.sso's `bodywt`). SS3's weight follows growth through the
quarter and the size of fish each fleet selects within an age. For fleets
whose catch is in numbers, w = 1.

The replays serve two purposes:

* **A check on the conversion.** The start-of-quarter replay with opal's
  weight does exactly what opal does. If opal matches it, opal is using the
  converted inputs as intended. @fig-o0 shows this ("replay, opal timing",
  from `ss3_bridge_replica()` in `shared/ss3-to-opal/`).
* **Attribution.** Every replay uses the same inputs and differs only in the
  catch step, so the differences between them (@tbl-timing, @fig-timing)
  are caused by when the catch is removed and at what weight. Nothing else
  differs, including growth, M, recruitment and selectivity. The replay
  that uses SS3's catch equation and SS3's fleet catch weights reproduces
  SS3 almost exactly. So with the same inputs, the catch step is the only
  thing separating opal's dynamics from SS3's.

The replays use SS3's selectivity-at-age, so they test the dynamics, not
opal's own selectivity curves (that is O2, @sec-fits).

```{r}
#| label: fig-o0
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "O0: opal at SS3's values against SS3 B1 (top: spawning biomass; bottom: relative to SS3). 'Replay, opal timing' is the start-of-quarter replay of @sec-replays with opal's weight, which opal matches exactly."
br = copy(opal_c$bridge)
br[, year := qtr_to_year(16 + ts)]
bl = rbind(br[, .(year, series = "SS3 B1", value = ss3)],
           br[, .(year, series = "opal (O0)", value = opal)],
           br[, .(year, series = "replay, opal timing", value = replica_opal)])
o0_col = c("SS3 B1" = "grey20", "opal (O0)" = "#7D3C98", "replay, opal timing" = "#CA6F1E")
p1 = ggplot(bl, aes(year, value, colour = series, linetype = series)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = o0_col) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "solid", "dashed")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Spawning biomass (t)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
p2 = ggplot(br, aes(year, rel_opal)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, colour = "#7D3C98") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "opal relative to SS3")
(p1 / p2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: timing-text
bar  = TM[grepl("Baranov", removal)]
pope = TM[grepl("Pope", removal)]
```

The first quarter agrees to `r pct(abs(br$rel_opal[1]), 2)`: the initial
age structure is converted directly. opal then drifts above SS3, to
`r pct(tail(br$rel_opal, 1))` by 2021 Q4. opal's spawning biomass matches the
replay of the converted inputs to `r sci(max(abs(br$opal / br$replica_opal - 1)), 0)`
(relative), which checks that opal uses the converted inputs as intended;
the difference from SS3 is in the dynamics. Two things
account for it: when the catch is taken within the quarter, and the weight
at which catch in weight is turned into numbers.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-timing
#| tbl-cap: "The replays of @sec-replays: spawning biomass relative to SS3 at SS3's parameter values, by when the catch is removed and the weight used to turn catch in weight into numbers. Every replay starts from opal's initial numbers-at-age (O0) and uses SS3's selectivity-at-age and recruitment, so they differ only in the catch step. The second row is opal's own calculation (it matches O0)."
tt = TM[, .(`2001-2021 mean` = pct(mean(rel[qtr_to_year(16 + ts) >= 2001]), 1),
            `2021 Q4` = pct(rel[.N], 1),
            `largest |diff|` = pct(max(abs(rel)), 2)), by = .(removal, weight)]
knitr::kable(tt, format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timing
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "The replays of @tbl-timing relative to SS3."
TM[, year := qtr_to_year(16 + ts)]
TM[, variant := paste0(removal, "; ", weight)]
ggplot(TM[ssb > 0], aes(year, rel, colour = variant)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 1.5)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative to SS3", colour = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

* **Catch weight.** SS3 turns catch in weight into numbers with each
  fleet's catch weight-at-age, which follows the fish's growth through the
  quarter and the fleet's selection within an age. Bigeye grow fast: an
  age-0 fish weighs `r fmt(100 * (opal_c$weights$mid[1] / opal_c$weights$beg[1] - 1), 0)`%
  more at mid-quarter than at the start. opal has one weight-at-age vector. At the
  start-of-quarter weight it removes so many young fish for the same tonnage
  that the population collapses at SS3's parameters; the mid-quarter weight
  (used here) and SS3's fleet catch weights give similar results.
* **Catch timing.** opal removes each quarter's catch at the start of the
  quarter, before natural mortality. SS3 removes it through the quarter
  (hybrid F), so part of the catch is fish that would otherwise have died.
  For the same catch opal leaves more fish alive, and with M of 0.48 per
  quarter at age 0 and the OBJ fisheries catching mostly fish under a year
  old, the difference accumulates. Removing the catch at mid-quarter (Pope's
  approximation) brings the replay to within
  `r pct(max(abs(pope$rel)), 0)` of SS3 over the series; SS3's catch
  equation with SS3's fleet catch weights reproduces SS3 to
  `r sci(max(abs(bar$rel)), 0)` (relative; the largest difference in any
  quarter).

# opal fits {#sec-fits}

Growth, h, sigma~R~, M, the biology and the initial F stay at SS3's values
(except in O1-F, @sec-init-f), as they are fixed in SS3 (except SD_young, held at SS3's estimate); opal's
default priors are switched off, as SS3 has no parameter priors. Both fits
estimate B~0~, the survey catchability, the main and late recruitment
deviations and the initial age structure; the last deviation, which belongs
to the quarter after the model, is fixed at 0.

* **O1** holds SS3's selectivity-at-age.
* **O2** estimates opal's own length-based double normals, started at SS3's
  curves, for the parameters SS3 estimates (the peak, top and widths of
  LL-n-A2 to A7, OBJ-A1 to A5 and the index); mirrors share their source's
  parameters. It starts from O1's estimates.
* **O1-noComp** is O1 with the compositions switched off (lambda 0), so
  the index and the recruitment and initial-deviation penalties inform it.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fits
#| tbl-cap: "Fits. The objective values are opal's and are not comparable with SS3's likelihood (different constants, and opal's compositions are predicted differently). Depletion is SSB / SSB0 in 2021 Q4. CPUE, compositions and recruitment are the negative log-likelihood terms opal reports (O1-noComp's composition term is reported but not in its objective, lambda 0); the objective also contains the initial-deviation penalty, and 'unreported' is the objective minus the sum of every weighted term opal reports (see @sec-limitations)."
fit_tab = copy(S)
fit_tab[, comp := ifelse(is.na(lp_lf), "", ifelse(lp_lf_in_objective %in% FALSE,
                                                   paste0(fmt(lp_lf, 1), " (not in objective)"), fmt(lp_lf, 1)))]
knitr::kable(fit_tab[, .(model, `n par` = n_par, objective = fmt(objective, 2),
                   `max gradient` = ifelse(is.na(max_gradient), "", sci(max_gradient, 1)),
                   `Hessian PD` = ifelse(is.na(positive_hessian), "", as.character(positive_hessian)),
                   `B0 (t)` = fmt(B0, 0), `SSB 2021 Q4 (t)` = fmt(ssb_end, 0),
                   depletion = fmt(depletion_end, 3),
                   CPUE = fmt(lp_cpue, 1), compositions = comp,
                   recruitment = fmt(lp_rec, 1), unreported = fmt(unreported, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: fits-text
o0 = S[model == "O0"]; o1 = S[model == "O1"]; o2 = S[model == "O2"]
nc = S[model == "O1-noComp"]; ss = S[model == "SS3 B1"]
conv = function(x) if (isTRUE(x$check_passes)) "converges and passes opal's fit check" else
    sprintf("does not converge (maximum gradient %s)", sci(x$max_gradient, 1))
```

O1 `r conv(o1)`. With SS3's selectivity fixed, opal's own optimum puts B~0~
at `r fmt(o1$B0, 0)` t (`r pct(o1$B0 / ss$B0 - 1)` above SS3's) and the
2021 Q4 depletion at `r fmt(o1$depletion_end, 3)`, against SS3's
`r fmt(ss$depletion_end, 3)`. That is close to where opal already sits at
SS3's values (O0, `r fmt(o0$depletion_end, 3)`): re-estimating the scale and
recruitment does not undo the catch-timing difference of @sec-o0, because
in opal's dynamics the same catches deplete the stock less. Without the
compositions (O1-noComp), the index and the recruitment and
initial-deviation penalties give a depletion of `r fmt(nc$depletion_end, 3)` (B~0~ `r fmt(nc$B0, 0)` t), so the
compositions push O1 towards a larger, less depleted stock.

O2 `r conv(o2)` and is shown for completeness only. Freeing opal's
selectivity improves the fit to the compositions by
`r fmt(o1$lp_lf - o2$lp_lf, 0)` units over O1, and its depletion of
`r fmt(o2$depletion_end, 3)` should not be read as an estimate.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fits
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass, depletion and age-0 recruitment: SS3 B1 and the opal fits."
tr = copy(opal_c$trajectory)
tr[, model := factor(model, levels = names(model_col))]
p1 = ggplot(tr, aes(year, ssb, colour = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SSB (t)", colour = NULL)
p2 = ggplot(tr, aes(year, depletion, colour = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SSB / SSB0", colour = NULL)
p3 = ggplot(tr[model != "O0"], aes(year, recruits, colour = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Age-0 recruits", colour = NULL)
(p1 / p2 / p3) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cpue

cp = copy(opal_c$cpue)
ggplot(cp, aes(year, pred, colour = model)) +
    geom_point(data = cp[model == "SS3 B1"], aes(year, obs), colour = "grey50", size = 0.6) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
```

# Estimating the initial F {#sec-init-f}

SS3 starts the population from an equilibrium fished at an initial F for
each fleet with an initial equilibrium catch. In this model those are
LL-n-A2 and OBJ-A5, with an arbitrary catch of 999 and lambda 0 on the
initial-catch likelihood, so their initial Fs are not tied to a catch; the
control file fixes them (phase -1) at `r sci(B[1, init_f_ll], 1)` and
`r sci(B[1, init_f_obj], 1)` per quarter, an almost unfished start. The
regime offset is what depletes the initial state in B0 (@sec-bridge).
opal has the same parameter (`log_init_F_f`, one per fishery, applied with
each fishery's selectivity in the initial equilibrium), and the conversion
carries SS3's values over as fixed. Neither model has an initial catch in its
likelihood, so the initial Fs are informed only by what the initial age
structure does to the index and the compositions. Three runs estimate them:

* **B0-F**: B0 (regime offset on) with both initial Fs estimated;
* **B1-F**: B1 (regime offset off) with both initial Fs estimated, the SS3
  counterpart of opal (which has no regime offset, so there is no opal run
  with the offset on);
* **O1-F**: opal O1 with the initial F of the same two fisheries estimated.

Each starts from its parent's estimates, with OBJ-A5's initial F moved off
~0 to 0.001. O1-F is also started from B1-F's estimates, and both starts
reach the same optimum (objectives
`r paste(fmt(opal_c$init_f_starts$objective, 3), collapse = " and ")`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-init-f
#| tbl-cap: "Estimating the initial F (per quarter; SS3's SE in brackets). Initial depletion is the SSB at the start of 1975 Q1 relative to unfished; final depletion is in 2021 Q4. SS3's NLL and opal's objective are not comparable with each other; compare within each model."
IF = bridge$init_f
fs = IF$summary
f_se = function(v, se) ifelse(is.na(se) | se == 0, sci(v, 1), sprintf("%s (%s)", sci(v, 1), sci(se, 1)))
ss3_init = IF$timeseries[era == "TIME", .SD[1], by = step]
fs[, init_dep := ss3_init$depletion[match(step, ss3_init$step)]]
ss3_tab = fs[, .(model = sub(" .*", "", label), `regime offset` = ifelse(regime == 0, "off", fmt(regime, 3)),
                 `initial F LL-n-A2` = f_se(init_f_ll, init_f_ll_se),
                 `initial F OBJ-A5` = f_se(init_f_obj, init_f_obj_se),
                 `NLL / objective` = fmt(nll, 2), `max gradient` = sci(max_gradient, 1),
                 `Hessian PD` = as.character(hessian_ok),
                 `SSB0 (t)` = fmt(ssb0, 0), `initial depletion` = fmt(init_dep, 3),
                 `final depletion` = fmt(depletion, 3))]
op_tab = S[model %in% c("O1", "O1-F"),
           .(model, `regime offset` = "none",
             `initial F LL-n-A2` = sci(init_f_ll, 1), `initial F OBJ-A5` = sci(init_f_obj, 1),
             `NLL / objective` = fmt(objective, 2), `max gradient` = sci(max_gradient, 1),
             `Hessian PD` = as.character(positive_hessian),
             `SSB0 (t)` = fmt(B0, 0), `initial depletion` = fmt(init_depletion, 3),
             `final depletion` = fmt(depletion_end, 3))]
knitr::kable(rbind(ss3_tab, op_tab), format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: init-f-text
b0 = fs[step == "00-base"]; b1 = fs[step == "01-no-regime"]
b0f = fs[step == "02-base-init-f"]; b1f = fs[step == "03-no-regime-init-f"]
o1 = S[model == "O1"]; o1f = S[model == "O1-F"]
gain_b1 = b1$nll - b1f$nll
lost = b1$nll - b0$nll
na = copy(IF$natage)
na[, rel := n / n[step == "00-base"], by = age]
na_old_b1f = na[step == "03-no-regime-init-f" & age >= 8, max(abs(rel - 1))]
na_old_b1  = na[step == "01-no-regime" & age >= 8, max(rel - 1)]
```

**With the regime offset on (B0-F)** the initial Fs add nothing: the
likelihood changes by `r fmt(b0$nll - b0f$nll, 3)` units, the offset stays
at `r fmt(b0f$regime, 2)`, OBJ-A5's initial F returns to its lower bound and
LL-n-A2's moves to `r sci(b0f$init_f_ll, 1)` with an SE of
`r sci(b0f$init_f_ll_se, 1)`, many times the estimate. With the offset
present the data cannot separate a lower initial recruitment from a
fished initial equilibrium, so the initial F is not estimable alongside it.

**Without the offset (B1-F)** the initial F does much of the offset's job.
The likelihood improves by `r fmt(gain_b1, 2)` of the `r fmt(lost, 2)` units
lost by removing the offset, through OBJ-A5's initial F
(`r sci(b1f$init_f_obj, 1)` per quarter, SE `r sci(b1f$init_f_obj_se, 1)`),
while LL-n-A2's goes to its lower bound. The initial depletion falls from
`r fmt(b1$init_dep, 3)` (B1) to `r fmt(b1f$init_dep, 3)`, against
`r fmt(b0$init_dep, 3)` in B0, and the 2021 Q4 depletion is
`r fmt(b1f$depletion, 3)` against `r fmt(b0$depletion, 3)` (B0) and
`r fmt(b1$depletion, 3)` (B1). The initial F also replaces most of the
negative early recruitment deviations B1 uses to lower its initial state
(their mean is `r fmt(b1f$early_dev_mean, 2)` in B1-F against
`r fmt(b1$early_dev_mean, 2)` in B1). B1-F's initial numbers-at-age match
B0's within `r pct(na_old_b1f, 0)` from age 8 quarters, where B1's are up to
`r pct(na_old_b1, 0)` above them. The two mechanisms still differ at the
youngest ages (@fig-init-natage): the offset lowers every initial age class
by the same factor, while the effect of an initial F builds up with the
number of quarters a cohort has been fished, so B1-F's youngest ages stay
above B0's. What the initial F does not recover
is the remaining `r fmt(b1f$nll - b0$nll, 2)` likelihood units.

**In opal (O1-F)** `r if (isTRUE(o1f$check_passes)) "the fit converges and passes opal's fit check" else sprintf("the fit does not pass opal's fit check (maximum gradient %s)", sci(o1f$max_gradient, 1))`.
The initial Fs are `r sci(o1f$init_f_ll, 1)` (LL-n-A2) and
`r sci(o1f$init_f_obj, 1)` (OBJ-A5) per quarter, an order of magnitude below
B1-F's for OBJ-A5, and the objective improves by only
`r fmt(o1$objective - o1f$objective, 3)` units on O1. The initial and
2021 Q4 depletions are `r fmt(o1f$init_depletion, 3)` and
`r fmt(o1f$depletion_end, 3)` (O1: `r fmt(o1$init_depletion, 3)` and
`r fmt(o1$depletion_end, 3)`), so in opal the initial F changes almost
nothing: O1 already starts from a nearly unfished state, and the
compositions that push O1 to a larger, less depleted stock (@sec-fits) give
no reason to deplete the initial state. The initial F is therefore not a
route to reproduce B0's initial state in opal while the catch-timing
difference remains. opal applies the initial F as a harvest
fraction at the start of the quarter, 1 - exp(-F), before natural mortality,
where SS3's initial equilibrium uses its catch equation; at these levels the
difference is small next to the catch-timing difference of @sec-o0, which
O1-F inherits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-init-f
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass relative to unfished: the SS3 runs with the initial F fixed (B0, B1) and estimated (B0-F, B1-F), and opal O1 and O1-F."
ts_f = IF$timeseries[era == "TIME", .(model = sub(" .*", "", label), year, depletion)]
tr_f = opal_c$trajectory[model %in% c("O1", "O1-F"), .(model, year, depletion)]
dd = rbind(ts_f, tr_f)
dd[, model := factor(model, levels = c("B0", "B0-F", "B1", "B1-F", "O1", "O1-F"))]
ggplot(dd, aes(year, depletion, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(B0 = "grey20", `B0-F` = "grey20", B1 = "#2471A3", `B1-F` = "#2471A3",
                                   O1 = "#C0392B", `O1-F` = "#C0392B")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(B0 = "solid", `B0-F` = "dashed", B1 = "solid", `B1-F` = "dashed",
                                     O1 = "solid", `O1-F` = "dashed")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SSB / SSB0", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-init-natage
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "SS3's numbers-at-age at the start of 1975 Q1 relative to the supplied model's (B0). Without the regime offset (B1) the older ages start about 50% higher; with the initial F estimated (B1-F) they are close to B0's again. B0-F is indistinguishable from B0."
na[, model := factor(sub(" .*", "", label), levels = c("B0", "B0-F", "B1", "B1-F"))]
ggplot(na[step != "00-base"], aes(age, rel, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`B0-F` = "grey20", B1 = "#2471A3", `B1-F` = "#2471A3")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`B0-F` = "dotted", B1 = "solid", `B1-F` = "dashed")) +
    labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Numbers / B0's numbers", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

# Limitations and differences from SS3 {#sec-limitations}

## Not available in opal

* **Within-step catch timing.** opal removes each time step's catch at its
  start. How much that matters depends on the mortality within a step
  (natural and fishing) and on how young the selected fish are, not on the
  step length alone: it is small when both are low. For this stock, with M
  of 0.48 per quarter at age 0 and large catches of young fish, it is the
  largest difference (@tbl-timing). A mid-step removal (Pope) would recover
  most of it, and SS3's catch equation nearly all of it.
* **Fishery-specific catch weight-at-age.** opal turns catch in weight into
  numbers with one weight-at-age vector for every fishery, at one time in the
  step. SS3 uses each fleet's catch weight-at-age, which accounts for growth
  through the step and for size selection within an age. A
  fishery-by-age catch weight (like the external selectivity matrix) would
  carry SS3's exactly.
* **Initial-equilibrium recruitment offset.** SS3's regime offset scales the
  initial equilibrium recruitment, unpenalised; opal has no equivalent, so B1
  removes it, which moves the whole trajectory (@sec-bridge). opal's initial
  deviations (`init_rdev_a`, one per initial age class) could carry B0's
  initial numbers-at-age exactly at SS3's values, but opal penalises them
  with sigma~R~ (about 10 likelihood units for an offset of -0.41 on 41
  ages), so a fit would pull the initial state back towards unfished. An
  unpenalised offset on the initial equilibrium (one parameter in opal's
  initial numbers) would let opal be converted from B0 directly. Estimating
  the initial F (B1-F, O1-F; @sec-init-f) recovers part of what the offset
  does, with a different initial age structure.
* **Age selectivity combined with size selectivity.** SS3 multiplies each
  fleet's length-based curve by an age curve (pattern 10: 0 at age 0;
  pattern 11 for the discards); opal has one or the other per fishery.
* **Conditional age-at-length data** (a few records, with lambda 0 in SS3).
* **A complete decomposition of the objective.** With the compositions in
  the likelihood, opal's objective is larger than the sum of the weighted
  terms it reports (by `r fmt(o1$unreported, 0)` units for O1; @tbl-fits),
  and the difference disappears when the compositions' lambda is 0, so part
  of what the composition likelihood contributes is not in the reported
  `lp_lf`. The NPO blue shark fits show the same. Until it is resolved, the
  reported terms cannot be added up to the objective, and composition
  likelihood comparisons between fits rest on the reported `lp_lf` only.

## Other structural differences and conversion choices

* **Plus-group length.** SS3 averages the plus group's length over the ages
  it accumulates; opal uses the growth curve at the oldest age
  (`r fmt(tail(G$laa_ss3, 1) - tail(G$laa_opal, 1), 2)` cm).
* **Observation timing.** SS3 predicts the fishery compositions from the
  catch through the quarter, with mid-quarter lengths, and the index in month
  1; opal predicts both from numbers and lengths at the start of the
  quarter.
* **Generalised size compositions** become opal's second composition bin
  scheme, with SS3's variance adjustments (mult_by_generalized_sizecomp).
* **Catchability.** SS3 solves it analytically (floating q); opal estimates
  it.
* **Late recruitment deviations.** SS3 estimates deviations for the two
  quarters after its last main deviation with the same sigma~R~ penalty;
  opal estimates them as ordinary deviations.

# Reproducing this document {.unnumbered}

| Step | Script | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scripts/01-build-ss3-bridge.r` | the SS3 bridge models and `vignettes/data/epo-bet-ss3-bridge-cache.rds` |
| 2 | `scripts/02-convert-fit-epo-bet-opal.r` | `vignettes/data/epo-bet-opal-cache.rds` and the fitted models |
| 3 | `quarto render vignettes/epo-bet-ss3-to-opal.qmd` | this document |

```{r}
#| label: session
cat(sprintf("Caches: bridge %s (SS3 %s); opal %s (opal %s, r4ss %s, R %s).\n",
            bridge$made_at, bridge$ss3_version, opal_c$created,
            opal_c$session$opal, opal_c$session$r4ss, opal_c$session$r))
```
